_about: Visitor-facing words for product slotting (Step 5). labels: grid headers for the slot columns, served by GET /api/loans/columns. terms: the glossary term behind each slot column's header tooltip. rules: one plain-English line per rule in backend/app/config/slotting.toml, keyed by the rule's name or reason, for the read-only Slotting rules popup. Definitions of terms live in content/glossary.json; the rules themselves, their numbers and sources live in slotting.toml and docs/public-sources.md. Everything is illustrative.

rules.Delinquent: Behind on payments (any MBA status other than Current). Agency pools take only current loans.
rules.Modified: The loan's terms were changed after a hardship. Modified loans do not go into new agency pools.
rules.Forbearance: The borrower is in, or recently left, a payment pause. Such loans wait until they are current again.
rules.UMBS: Conventional and High-Balance loans go into Uniform MBS, issued by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.
rules.Ginnie Mae II: FHA, VA and USDA loans go into Ginnie Mae II pools, backed by the US government.
rules.Whole loan: Jumbo and Non-QM loans fall outside the agencies' rules and are sold whole to banks and investors.
rules.UMBS High-LTV: Refinances above 125 LTV go into their own specified pools, not TBA.
rules.UMBS 30 High-Balance: 30-year High-Balance loans. A TBA pool may hold only a small share of them, so they get their own slot.
rules.UMBS 15 High-Balance: 15-year High-Balance loans, kept apart for the same reason.
rules.UMBS 30: 30-year fixed-rate conventional loans: the most traded TBA product.
rules.UMBS ARM: SOFR ARMs go into ARM pools, which do not trade TBA, so they get no coupon ladder.
rules.G2 30: 30-year fixed-rate FHA, VA and USDA loans.
